headline: Education minister regrets remarks amid student protests
summary: Students are demanding the minister's resignation after protests against HSC exams being held in adverse weather conditions.
details: Students across Dhaka have staged massive protests, blocking major roads including the Dhaka-Tangail highway and Manik Mia Avenue, demanding the resignation of the Education Minister.
The demonstrations are sparked by the decision to conduct Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations during adverse weather conditions, which students claim is unfair and difficult.
Protesters marched from Science Lab toward the Parliament building, where they held a sit-in and chanted slogans against the ministry.
Police intervened at the Parliament building, using batons to disperse the students and clear the area.
Following the unrest and widespread criticism, the Education Minister has expressed regret over his previous remarks regarding the situation.
The protests have caused severe traffic gridlock across the capital city, with authorities urging commuters to use alternative routes.
caption:
Traffic gridlock in Dhaka as students demand the Education Minister's resignation.

Students across Dhaka have staged massive protests, blocking major roads including the Dhaka-Tangail highway and Manik Mia Avenue, demanding the resignation of the Education Minister.

Protesters marched from Science Lab toward the Parliament building, where they held a sit-in and chanted slogans against the ministry.

Police intervened at the Parliament building, using batons to disperse the students and clear the area.

Following the unrest and widespread criticism, the Education Minister has expressed regret over his previous remarks regarding the situation.

The protests have caused severe traffic gridlock across the capital city, with authorities urging commuters to use alternative routes.

headline: Govt may hold re-examinations for flood-hit HSC examinees
summary: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Milon announced that the government is ready to organize re-exams for students who missed their tests due to floods.
details: Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Milon stated that the government is prepared to hold re-examinations for HSC students who were unable to participate in their exams due to ongoing seasonal rains and floods.
The Minister informed Parliament on Tuesday in response to a supplementary question from MP Md. Shafiqul Islam of Patuakhali-2.
He noted that the Ministry of Education has been monitoring all examination centers across the country around the clock during the monsoon season.
To ensure students can take their exams without disruption, local administrations have been instructed to immediately relocate centers if floodwaters enter the premises.

The Minister highlighted that while significant problems occurred at Comilla Government College due to flooding, authorities quickly moved centers in other affected areas to ensure necessary arrangements.
He clarified that if any student misses an exam due to administrative errors following floodwater entry into an institution, the government will review the case and arrange re-exams if necessary.
Minister Milon mentioned that similar arrangements have already been made under the Chattogram Education Board and such opportunities will remain available in the future.
He urged students to focus on their studies, emphasizing that the government is more concerned about the smooth organization of exams than the students themselves.
The Minister reaffirmed that the government will not allow students to be deprived of their rights due to any mistakes or deficiencies in the organization of the exams.
caption:
Will you miss your HSC exam due to floods? The government is ready to hold re-exams.
